panels.rationale: Clinical photograph of a term infant showing uncovered eviscerated bowel through a right paraumbilical abdominal wall defect, consistent with simple gastroschisis. The caption explicitly identifies the defect location and the article identifies the presentation as gastroschisis. [raw subtype: simple gastroschisis]

panels.figure_caption: Term infant with simple gastroschisis. The picture shows a small abdominal wall defect to the right of the site of umbilical cord insertion.
in_text_mentions: The International Clearinghouse for Birth Defects Surveillance and Research defines gastroschisis (Figure 1) as “a congenital malformation characterized by visceral herniation usually through a right side abdominal wall defect to an intact umbilical cord and not covered by a membrane” [3]. Approximately 10% of infants with gastroschisis have intestinal stenosis or atresia [4] resulting from vascular insufficiency due to a volvulus or compression of vascular pedicle by a narrowing abdominal ring [5].
